newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB says India deal is earliest new crop sale ever.
newsitem.headline: AWB says India deal is earliest new crop sale ever.

text.p: Australia's latest sale of wheat to India was the earliest sale of new crop wheat in the country's history, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in a statement.
Of the one million tonnes of wheat sold, 750,000 tonnes was from the new crop which was not yet in the ground, AWB general manager international Nigel Officer said.
"That forward selling provides an extremely good hedge against any negative price movements later this year," he said.
The AWB's earliest sale of new crop wheat in the past typically has been in August and September, he said.

Australia has now sold 2.325 million tonnes of wheat to India and with the exception of small parcels sold by Canada and Argentina, Australia has done about 90 percent of India's imports this year, he said.
"The latest sale confirms our preferred supplier status and follows strong sales in 1992 and sales earlier this year, he said.

"We are delighted to be able to develop this business with India at a time when we have a record crop and at a time when China, usually a big buyer, is not in the market because of its own good crop," he said.
Officer, who said the international grain market did not expect India to import wheat this year, valued the sales for the year at about A$500 million.
"That's a great windfall in unanticipated business for Australia," he said.

"The latest sale, which will be shipped during the second half of the year, was finalised after a recent visit to Delhi by the AWB and positions us extremely well for long-term business with India," he said.
"We continue to discuss further business opportunities with India, and that's not just in wheat. Pulses are a significant growth opportunity there for Australian producers," he said.
With the latest one million tonne Indian sale, the AWB has now committed more than 70 percent of projected exports this year.
"With tonnages already committed to regular buyers, we are in an extremely tight supply situation," Officer said.
"This puts us in a very strong position to selectively target our limited unallocated stocks to high returning buyers," he said.
